svg.title: DRDebug — compare failure patterns with targeted corrections
svg.desc: A full ten-line Masked Softmax pseudocode block on the left collects independent defects; the right shows the corresponding correct implementation. Six arrows identify row addressing, row masks and padding, masked maximum, exponential stabilization, reduction axis and accumulator precision. Cross-tile normalization is a separate alternative below. This is a composite illustration, not one recorded repair run. All code, arrows and correction sites remain visible in this static overview.

g.text: Keep the implementation. Correct the failing steps.
One kernel. Multiple ways to go wrong.
Follow the highlighted correction and its explanation below.
Same computation, corrected at the source
stride=rows advances by the row count, so the next row loads the wrong values.
stride=cols restores the correct row start before any arithmetic.
02 / Two masking errors, one correction site
A shared mask can select the wrong items; zero-filled padding still adds weight.
Use each row’s mask and −INF to exclude invalid positions before normalization.
Padding’s raw 0 can outrank valid scores near −104, so valid exponentials underflow.
Take max(s) after masking; the valid exponentials remain representable in this input.
Without the shift, exp(90) becomes Inf; exp(−104) rounds to zero in FP32.
Subtract the row maximum to preserve relative weights and avoid these NaN-producing extremes.
axis=0 mixes rows, giving each column a cross-batch denominator.
Reduce axis=−1 instead: each row uses the sum of its own exponentials.
Sequential FP16 rounding stalls at 2,048 when summing 4,096 ones.
Accumulate in FP32 to reach 4,096; keep the final output FP16.
FP16 input/output · FP32 internal · per-row normalization
Constructed illustration: independent failure patterns shown together, not one recorded repair.
Each defect is evaluated separately. Real kernels require independent NPU validation.
Explore the inputs and evidence on the website ↗
